text.p: FoxMeyer Health Corp. said Monday it was suing McKesson Corp. and a dozen major pharmaceutical manufacturers for allegedly conspiring to drive its subsidiary, FoxMeyer Drug Co., out of business.
In the suit filed in a Texas District Court, FoxMeyer seeks compensatory damages of more than $400 million, as well as punitive damages which could amount to $1 billion or more.

FoxMeyer said the complaint alleged that McKesson "misused confidential financial and competitive information to which it had gained access in conceiving, perpetrating, and promoting a plan to drive FoxMeyer out of its industry."
FoxMeyer Drug, a drug distributor, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in August.

The suit accuses McKesson of exploiting information by "interfering with FoxMeyer Drug's customer and vendor relationships and disrupting its operations" as part of a plan to acquire the company "at a significantly distressed price."

FoxMeyer said other defendants include pharmaceutical manufacturers Pfizer Inc., Bristol-Myers Squibb Co., Glaxo Wellcome Plc, Eli Lilly & Co., American Home Products Corp. unit Wyeth Ayerst Laboratories Inc., Hoechst AG's Hoechst Marion Rousell Inc., Schering-Plough Corp., Amgen Inc., SmithKline Beecham Plc, Zeneca Group Plc, Johnson & Johnson's Janssen Pharmaceuticals Inc., and Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc.
All of those companies are suppliers to FoxMeyer Drug Co.
McKesson and the other companies named in the suit were not immediately available for comment.
FoxMeyer's stock was unchanged at $1.625, while McKesson fell 87.5 cents to $52.50 on the New York Stock Exchange in late trading.
